narrative: On 31 January 2017 a GitLab engineer accidentally ran rm against the primary PostgreSQL data directory while attempting to resync a secondary, deleting approximately 300 GB of production data before the command was halted two minutes later.
root_cause: None of the five planned recovery mechanisms (pg_dump, LVM snapshot, Azure disk snapshot, streaming replication, S3 upload) were in a state that met the recovery point objective, so restoration required a six-hour-old LVM snapshot from a secondary.
impact_bullets: 700 new-user signups during the window unrecoverable
lesson_domain_bullets: Backup mechanisms must be exercised as often as the RPO demands
Destructive commands need blast-radius guards at the shell layer
